objectives: Describe the causes and effects of deforestation, soil erosion, desertification, pollution and climate change
Explain how these problems can be managed
reviewNotes: Teacher to verify statements about Lake Chad (shrinkage), the effects of deforestation on rainfall and the examples of conservation areas; keep language balanced and non-political.
Syllabus references and scope to be checked against the official GCE Board syllabus; all facts, names and figures to be verified by a geography teacher before release.

blocks.md: **Deforestation** is the clearing of forests for farming, timber, fuelwood or building. It destroys habitats, reduces biodiversity, exposes soil to erosion, reduces rainfall in the long term and releases carbon dioxide. It is a serious problem in the forests of southern Cameroon. **Soil erosion** is the removal of topsoil by water or wind, often on steep slopes and bare land.

items.text: A chain of cause and effect

blocks.caption: How deforestation can lead to hunger
blocks.alt: Four boxes linked by arrows: logging, bare soil, erosion and floods, poor harvests.

blocks.md: **Desertification** is the spread of desert-like conditions on the margins of deserts, such as the Sahel. Causes: drought, overgrazing, cutting trees for fuel and bad farming. Effects: poor harvests, hunger and migration. Lake Chad has shrunk greatly over the decades, which has affected fishermen, farmers and herders around it.

blocks.title: Pollution and climate change
blocks.md:
- **Water pollution:** waste, chemicals and sewage in rivers cause disease.
- **Air pollution:** smoke and exhaust fumes, bush burning.
- **Land pollution:** plastic and waste that is not collected.
- **Climate change:** greenhouse gases (carbon dioxide, methane) trap heat, raising the average temperature; effects include changes in rainfall, droughts, floods and rising sea level, which threatens low coasts.

blocks.title: Management
blocks.md: Plant trees and protect forests; manage logging and use fuel-saving stoves; terrace slopes and use cover crops to stop erosion; create national parks and reserves; collect and recycle waste and treat sewage; use clean energy; and educate people and enforce environmental laws. Sustainable development meets present needs without harming the future.

blocks.title: Be careful
blocks.md:
- Natural hazards (floods, landslides, drought) become disasters when people are unprepared or have built in dangerous places.
- Deforestation has many causes; do not say only 'logging'.
- Climate change and the ozone hole are different problems.

blocks.title: Example 1: cause and effect
blocks.statement: Explain how clearing forest on a steep slope can lead to flooding downstream.
steps: Without tree cover rain falls directly on the soil and runs off quickly.
Soil is washed into rivers and raises the river beds.
Rivers overflow more easily after heavy rain.
blocks.answer: Fast runoff and silted rivers cause floods.

blocks.title: Example 2: management
blocks.statement: Name two ways a community on a hillside can reduce soil erosion.
steps: Terracing slows the flow of water down the slope.
Planting trees and cover crops protect soil with roots and leaves.
blocks.answer: Terracing and planting trees or cover crops.
